title: Salesforce Seals $5.66 Billion Braze Deal, Sending BRZE Shares Up 50%【CNBC】
body:
Salesforce Co. disclosed on Tuesday that it will acquire customer‑engagement platform Braze Inc. in a cash transaction valued at roughly $5.66 billion, translating to $47.50 per Braze share. The announcement sent Braze’s stock soaring more than 50 percent in after‑hours trading, while Salesforce’s own shares slipped about 1 percent in early market activity.

The deal, slated to close in Salesforce’s fiscal 2028, marks the cloud‑software giant’s most significant foray into the fast‑growing marketing‑technology (MarTech) space since its purchase of Tableau and Slack. Braze, a San Francisco‑based provider of real‑time, omnichannel messaging solutions, has built a client roster that includes major consumer brands such as Disney, Peloton and HBO Max. By integrating Braze’s capabilities, Salesforce aims to deepen its Customer 360 suite and offer marketers a more seamless path from data capture to personalized outreach across email, push notifications, in‑app messages and SMS.

Analysts view the acquisition as a strategic response to intensifying competition from Adobe, Microsoft and a wave of specialist MarTech firms that have been chipping away at Salesforce’s market share in the customer‑experience segment. “The price tag reflects both Braze’s impressive growth trajectory and the premium Salesforce is willing to pay to lock in a best‑in‑class engagement engine,” noted Karen Liu, a senior technology analyst at Forrester. Braze reported a 35 percent year‑over‑year revenue increase in its most recent quarter, driven by expanding subscription revenue and a surge in demand for real‑time, AI‑enhanced messaging. The cash‑only structure of the deal also signals Salesforce’s confidence in its balance sheet, which remains robust after a series of strategic divestitures and cost‑optimization initiatives.

From a financial perspective, the transaction will be financed primarily through Salesforce’s ample cash reserves, supplemented by a modest amount of new debt issuance. The company expects the acquisition to be accretive to earnings per share within two years, assuming the integration proceeds without major disruption. However, some investors expressed concern that the $47.50 per‑share premium—about 45 percent above Braze’s closing price prior to the rumor—could pressure short‑term profitability. Moreover, the integration of a fast‑moving SaaS platform into Salesforce’s larger, more bureaucratic structure poses execution risk, particularly around maintaining Braze’s culture of rapid product iteration.

Regulatory approval appears likely, as the merger does not raise significant antitrust red flags. Nonetheless, the deal will be scrutinized by shareholders of both companies. Braze’s board has recommended the offer, emphasizing the strategic fit and the opportunity for shareholders to realize immediate value. Salesforce’s shareholders, meanwhile, will watch closely for any impact on the company’s long‑term growth rate, especially as the broader tech sector navigates a period of elevated interest rates and cautious capital allocation.

Looking ahead, the integration of Braze is expected to accelerate Salesforce’s push into AI‑driven, real‑time customer engagement—a domain where competitors are already deploying generative‑AI tools to personalize experiences at scale. If executed effectively, the acquisition could position Salesforce as the de facto platform for end‑to‑end customer journeys, from data ingestion to omnichannel activation. The next few quarters will reveal how quickly Salesforce can meld Braze’s technology and talent into its ecosystem, and whether the move will translate into sustained revenue uplift and market‑share gains in the increasingly crowded MarTech arena.
